newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Manslaughter trial for UK surgeon opens in NZ.
newsitem.headline: Manslaughter trial for UK surgeon opens in NZ.

text.p: A British heart surgeon pleaded not guilty in a Wellington court to three charges of manslaughter when his trial opened on Tuesday.
The 44-year-old surgeon is charged with the deaths of three patients he operated on when working in a Christchurch hospital in 1991 and 1992, and with falsifying their death certificates.
The Liverpool doctor returned to New Zealand after an extradition battle lasting 2-1/2 years.
The charges allege that Keith Ramstead caused the deaths of an elderly woman and two men by failing to use reasonable knowledge, skill and care in surgical treatment, thereby committing manslaughter.
Dressed in a dark suit and looking pale, the slightly built surgeon pleaded not guilty to all charges in a strong clear voice.
The trial, transferred from Christchurch to Wellington at Ramstead's request, was delayed as the judge heard and rejected a plea for television cameras to be allowed in court.

The charges relate to three elderly Christchurch people, Pieter van Dijk, who died on December 3, 1991, Arthur William Wilkinson, who died on June 4, 1992, and Nancie Muncie, who died on August 24, 1992.
All three died on the operating table during surgery for cancer.

Prosecutor Brent Stanaway told the court in his opening address that after the operations on Wilkinson and van Dijk, Ramstead had contacted the Christchurch coroner's office. He had said he would certify the cause of death in a bid to ensure there would be no inquiry, Stanaway said.
When Muncie died, Ramstead had telephoned the coroner and told him he was would certify the cause of death as a heart attack, the prosecutor said.
The trial is expected to last a month.
